title: Let us join the angel's greeting

edition.locus: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia, Latin column, In annuntiationem Sermo I, printed p. 12, cols. C-D (PDF p. 36)

source_text: Agite igitur, carissimi, et nos angelicam consectantes laudem, debitum pro viribus grati persolvamus, dicentes: Ave ac gaude, gratia plena, Dominus tecum. Tuum enim vere est avere, atque gaudere: quoniam tecum divina gratia, ut novit, habitationem elegit: cum ancilla, Rex gloriae: cum speciosa, speciosus forma prae filiis hominum: cum impolluta, qui sanctificat universa. Tecum Deus, et ex te Deus, ac perfectus homo, in quo omnis plenitudo divinitatis inhabitat.
pass_a_gloss: Come (agite) therefore, dearest (carissimi), and we, following (consectantes) the angelic praise (angelica laus), the debt (debitum) of a grateful one (grati) according to our strength (pro viribus) let us pay (persolvamus), saying: Hail (ave) and rejoice (gaude), full of grace, the Lord with you. For yours truly it is to fare well (avere) and to rejoice (gaudere): since with you divine grace, as it knows (ut novit), has chosen (elegit) a dwelling (habitatio): with the handmaid (ancilla), the King of glory (Rex gloriae): with the beautiful one (speciosa), the one beautiful in form beyond the sons of men (speciosus forma prae filiis hominum): with the undefiled one (impolluta), He who sanctifies (sanctificat) all things. With you God, and from you God, and perfect man (perfectus homo), in whom all the fullness of divinity (plenitudo divinitatis) dwells (inhabitat).

choices.issue: in quo omnis plenitudo divinitatis inhabitat
choices.choice: 'in quo omnis plenitudo divinitatis inhabitat' quotes Colossians 2:9; cited.
'Tuum ... est avere, atque gaudere' plays on Ave (from avere, 'to fare well'); rendered 'to fare well and to rejoice'.
'Rex gloriae' may recall Psalm 24:7-10 and 'ancilla' Luke 1:38; stock titles here, not cited.
'debitum ... grati' rendered 'the debt of thanks' (margin 'al. grato animo', 'with a grateful heart', gives the same sense).

pass_b_english: Come then, beloved, and let us too, following the angel's praise, pay as far as we are able the debt of thanks, saying: Hail and rejoice, full of grace, the Lord is with you (Luke 1:28). For it is truly yours to fare well and to rejoice, since divine grace, as it knows how, has chosen its dwelling with you: with the handmaid, the King of glory; with the beautiful one, He who is fair in form beyond the sons of men (Psalm 45:2); with the undefiled, He who sanctifies all things. With you is God, and from you is God, and perfect man, in whom all the fullness of the Godhead dwells (Colossians 2:9).

'Tuum ... est avere, atque gaudere' plays on Ave (from avere, 'to fare well'); rendered 'to fare well and to rejoice'. 'Rex gloriae' may recall Psalm 24:7-10 and 'ancilla' Luke 1:38; stock titles here, not cited. 'debitum ... grati' rendered 'the debt of thanks' (margin 'al. grato animo', 'with a grateful heart', gives the same sense).
